[b]Operation Nightfall Vengeance  The First Strike

March 18, 2025  02:00 Hours
Over Sal-Baliz Airspace[/b]

The desert stretched endlessly below, a sea of sand broken only by the occasional rocky outcrop or faint traces of dirt roads. In the darkness, the enemy was invisible, but we knew they were there. Missile sites. Supply convoys. The infrastructure that fueled Sal-Balizs war machine.

Tonight, we struck first.

"Albatross Squadron, check-in."

I adjusted my grip on the controls, heart steady but alert. "Albatross-2, all systems green." One by one, the rest of the bomber squadron reported in. To our flanks, Viper and Ghost Fighter Squadrons kept formation, scanning the ground below for anti-air threats.

"AWACS Skywatch to Albatross Squadronyou are approaching target zone. Enemy radar is active. They know you're coming."

Of course, they did. We were the first bombers in Etherniastis history to cross into Sal-Baliz airspace on an offensive mission. This was no routine patrol. This was war.

A burst of light from the groundthen another. Anti-air batteries opened fire, sending up a wall of burning tracers. The sky erupted in chaos, red-hot rounds slicing through the night, looking for us.

"Flak! Stay in formation! Fighters, clear those batteries!"

Viper Squadron peeled off, diving toward the enemy below. A second later, air-to-ground missiles streaked down, followed by fireballs blooming along the sand. The first defenses had been hit, but more were lighting up along the desert roads.

"Albatross Squadron, target confirmed. Begin bombing run."

I lined up my targeting systems. The crosshairs blinked over key objectivessupply convoys, hardened bunkers, storage depots. The kind of things that, if destroyed, would make the enemy fight on empty stomachs and dry fuel tanks.

One breath. One moment.

"Payload away."

Silence. Then fire and thunder.

The ground shattered, sending shockwaves through the desert. I saw convoys scatter, storage tanks burst into flames, and secondary explosions rip through enemy supply lines.

"Direct hit! Targets neutralized. All bombers, RTB! Fighters, cover our exit!"

We pulled away, our payloads delivered, our mission complete. The war had begunbut now, Sal-Baliz knew what was coming.

Tonight, Etherniasti had drawn first blood.

[quote=the_crystalline_empire;58826029]Queen Drs would listen intently, her piercing brown eyes staring at the minister as she droned on, after a few moments of silence and a few whispers amongst those staffers on the Thrømm side the queen would speak, her words tight and tinged with nobility, posh yet not prickish.

"It has long been our goal back in Thýven to ensure the strategic White Sea was held strongly against any foreign attacks, given that we own most of the islands in the sea, minus the Austmark, it would be strategic at best to accept this deal, given the fact that it is dangerous for only one nation to hold the full power while the other makes deals behind the back of many to undermine ones power over the sea."

She paused.

"I will accept on behalf of the government, but I must see the details for this alliance and its purposes," she continued as more mutters went among the Thrømm staffers, usually the queen never stepped out of her bounds of smiling and waving and dealing with parliament with a seven foot pole, distance was her name, but it seemed that she had done the unprecedented for her reign thusfar, she had drawn the matter close to her, and closed the need for parliament in the situation. It was a dangerous and calculated move to ensure swift conclusion and not drawn out months of waiting for parliament to make up its mind. [/quote]
"Details?... well, nothing you haven't heard before." Ostman said, her tone slowly raising itself to a blanketing bellow. "The Commonwealth of High Albany is one of the most powerful nations in Vespuria today, and yet it knows not what to do with its own capabilities. I am sure that Thýven presents itself as the same on Elseyr."

The Minister raised herself from her seat and turned to a large projection on the screen, which would load up a map of the nations overlooking the White Sea.

"Therefore, the Commonwealth proposes that we join ourselves together in a peaceable alliance, in the name of collective security but also collective action. Unlike THEP, we do not believe in enforcing costly conflicts on the other side of Erene. We only mandate one thing, that the White Sea remain in our hands and not in the hands of these new powers that seem to be springing up left, right, and center."

The Albic delegation murmured as Ostman flicked through the slides of the projection, listing down the specifics. Collective security, equipment standardization, intelligence-sharing, crisis response, peacekeeping, it was all included in their overarching framework. However, one thing would stick out from among the provisions of the alliance: The concept of joint action, that wars must be fought by the alliance under the alliance's own flag, not under the flag of its member nations.

"I'm sure the more conservative members of your government may be reluctant to accept this aspect of the alliance, Your Majesty." Ostman cautioned. "And yet, we believe it'll be most pertinent for the alliance to fight as a single, cohesive unit. We're in the middle of a new decade now, and we must ensure that every single element in our military capabilities is subsumed into a unified system. You've seen THEP's disjointed and fragmentary sorties against Sal-Baliz territory. That alone will not protect our interests in the White Sea."
